opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin is within policy. Recommend admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E001 (Anita Young) as a contractor with basic security training. As a contractor without advanced training, she is not eligible for admin or write on Payroll; maximum permitted is read. Recommend read, not admin.
reason: Anita Young (E001) is requesting admin access to Payroll. Per the HR record (looked up in HR's own database), she is a full-time employee whose role is Payroll Specialist. Since Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, a full-time employee in that role may have admin under policy. The requested level (admin) is within policy, so grant admin. (Note: the Security note lists her as a contractor with basic training, which conflicts with the HR employment record; I am relying on the HR record for employment type, which makes her eligible for admin.)
